event.summary: Retired container confinement removal is guarded and specified
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR: investigated whether removing checkout confinement lets retired container sessions read outside host files. No such route is established: inspect_download loads the stored launch then require_active_launch refuses before resolve_path or inspect. Source: service/core.rs:3731-3739 rejects container::is_retired; container.rs:18-22 identifies any agent selection with container.is_some(), preserving the previous branch's predicate. terminals.rs:911 applies the same guard before terminal resolution; uploads.rs:943 applies it before staging. Suggested bucket if route existed: highest/security; could-be-highest: yes, original suspected host-file disclosure retained here. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for assigned file-access change. proposed_drop: source predicate is equivalent to removed container branch and refusal precedes filesystem access; additionally SPEC_impl.md:4093-4095 explicitly states: 'Container environments use these ordinary file rules against their in-container supervisor. The earlier checkout-confinement browser adapter and supervisor checks belong to the retired supervisor-outside model and are removed with its terminal access.' SPEC_impl.md:8647-8650 says: 'A retired session supports Delete only. Refuse all other lifecycle, terminal and exec paths, including plain Replace.' possible_cover: none. No execution performed. This closes the initial authority lead; it does not claim every unrelated service entrypoint was reviewed.

event.summary: File requests retain retired-launch refusal and in-container authority
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR: removing old checkout confinement does not establish the suspected path from a retired container session to outside-host files. Later-turn synthesis traced admission and routing as well as the local guard. Details: connection.rs:613-616 routes session-authenticated controls through handle_restricted_control, whose catch-all at handlers.rs:3611-3621 refuses operations outside its allowlist; file stat/download are not allowed there. Full-authority StatFile and BeginDownload dispatch at connection.rs:690-704 to downloads::stat/start. Both independently call inspect_download (downloads.rs:190 and :220); :60-65 reads the stored session launch and rejects retired launches via core.rs:3731-3739/container.rs:18-22 before path expansion, canonicalization or open. Upload admission also rejects retired sessions before creating a transfer route (handlers.rs:2625-2654), and stage_claimed rechecks under the lifecycle claim before creating filesystem state (uploads.rs:920-947). Ordinary container environment hosts instead resolve through access.rs:397-427 to RemoteRoute::PodmanExec using the registered container's confirmed identity and login user. access.rs:196-234 lowers the payload to podman exec -i with that identity after --, and transport.rs:198-238 executes the supervisor stdio command through that route. Therefore the ordinary supervisor's account-wide file read runs inside its container namespace; the physical container host supervisor is not used as a file relay. Contract: SPEC_impl.md:4093-4095 says 'Container environments use these ordinary file rules against their in-container supervisor. The earlier checkout-confinement browser adapter and supervisor checks belong to the retired supervisor-outside model and are removed with its terminal access.' SPEC_impl.md:8647-8650 requires Delete-only retirement and refusal of other terminal/exec paths. Suggested bucket if the original suspected outside-host disclosure route existed: highest/security; could-be-highest: yes, original suspected consequence retained. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of this assigned file-confinement concern, no execution performed. proposed_drop: equivalent retired-launch predicate plus pre-filesystem refusal, restricted request admission, and explicit in-container transport preserve the authority boundary. possible_cover: caller reports g079/g096/g097 independently agree on legacy launch/attachment refusal; no coverage search performed. Caveats: this does not settle the separate g074 constructed-peer/TCP/cache concern or claim every service request is safe; it assumes the ordinary Podman namespace and authenticated helm connection described by the product contract. No readily checkable premise remains open for this file-specific candidate.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: checked whether removing the output cleanup watch can leave output running or deadlock a terminal detach. event.summary: Missing-terminal docs describe the pre-migration lifecycle
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: the maintenance documentation teaches that an old terminal is missing because it was already absent when a supervisor restarted. This release deliberately ends all old terminals and discards their screen, even when an ended agent's terminal was still present; readers following the helper's explanation get the wrong lifecycle model. Details: terminals.rs:828-845 describes every non-interrupted case as a 'restart gap' where 'its tmux session was already gone' and says the sentence 'names the restart and nothing about the agent'. The changed implementation at :862-875 instead says an update ended the old terminal and offers a new one. SPEC.md:3003-3016 explicitly requires ending all old terminals at first startup, retaining already-ended agents' outcomes but removing their screens; SPEC_impl.md:2979-2983 requires reload to take every old-kind row as terminal-less without probing its recorded pane. The comment should describe deliberate retirement for tmux rows and reserve runtime absence/unavailability for terminal-host rows, while preserving the rule not to infer when an agent exited from Interrupted. Suggested bucket: other/documentation correctness. Confidence: confirmed by source and contracts; no incorrect runtime behavior or direct user-facing malfunction established. could-be-highest: no. proposed_drop: false; prior exclusion based solely on absent user-facing harm is withdrawn because documentation correctness is in scope. possible_cover: none. No execution performed. Original consequence retained: stale explanatory context can mislead future readers; the shipped refusal wording and changed test themselves follow the intended migration behavior.

event.summary: Missing-terminal docs describe the pre-migration lifecycle
event.detail: Reviewed commit: dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4. TLDR: maintenance documentation attributes old-terminal absence to a failed survival across supervisor restart, rather than this release's deliberate terminal retirement, and describes Interrupted as boot-classifier evidence even though migration also assigns it. Details: terminals.rs:817-833 says an entry loses its terminal when reloaded without a surviving tmux session; its two cases call Interrupted boot-id classification and every other case a 'restart gap', saying the terminal 'was already gone' and the refusal 'names the restart and nothing about the agent'. This changes interpretation: a maintainer could infer that terminal presence is still probed and that Interrupted identifies a reboot. Actual source core.rs:6965-6969 unconditionally maps TerminalKind::Tmux to None without looking up its address; :7097-7114 assigns Transition::TerminalEnded to old rows last launching, running or stopping even without a reboot, while ended rows retain outcomes. The changed refusal at terminals.rs:862-875 correctly names an update ending an old terminal and offers a new one. SPEC.md:3003-3016 explicitly requires first-start retirement and loss of old screens; SPEC_impl.md:2979-2983 requires unconditional terminal absence on reload. Revise the helper docs and nearby resolution comment to describe retirement for old-kind rows and the boot-or-retirement meaning of Interrupted, while retaining the rule not to infer when the agent actually exited.
